sidebar:
7.1 Sidebar & Navigation – Overview

The sidebar is the central navigation element of the ABpE portal. It is dynamically built from the configured modules and the base navigation. The sidebar is responsive and adapts to different screen sizes.

7.2 Structure of the Sidebar

The sidebar consists of three areas:

  1. Main Navigation: Dashboard + all active modules (from module.json)
  2. Separator (visual)
  3. System Navigation: Admin, API Docs, Logout

7.3 Context Processor for Navigation

The context processor navigation() in context_processors.py provides the navigation for the sidebar. It combines the base navigation from modules.json with the modules from the scanner.

def navigation(request):
    # Load base navigation
    with open('modules.json') as f:
        base_config = json.load(f)
    
    # Load modules from scanner
    module_nav = scanner.get_navigation()
    
    # Main navigation: Dashboard + modules
    main_nav = [base_config['dashboard']] + module_nav
    
    # System navigation
    system_nav = base_config.get('system', [])
    
    return {
        'main_navigation': main_nav,
        'system_navigation': system_nav,
    }

7.4 Sidebar Template

The sidebar template (sidebar.html) renders the navigation generically:

<div class="sidebar" id="sidebar">
    <div class="mt-3">
        {% for item in main_navigation %}
        <a href="{{ item.route }}"
           class="nav-link {% if active_module == item.id %}active{% endif %}"
           data-module="{{ item.id }}">
            <i class="bi bi-{{ item.icon }}"></i>
            <span data-i18n="{{ item.id }}">{{ item.title }}</span>
        </a>
        
        {# Show subpages when active #}
        {% if item.subpages and active_module == item.id %}
        <div class="submenu ms-4">
            {% for subpage in item.subpages %}
            <a href="{{ subpage.route }}" class="nav-link subpage-link">
                <i class="bi bi-arrow-right-short"></i>
                <span>{{ subpage.title }}</span>
            </a>
            {% endfor %}
        </div>
        {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
    </div>
    
    <hr class="mx-3">
    
    <div>
        {% for item in system_navigation %}
        <a href="{{ item.route }}" class="nav-link">
            <i class="bi bi-{{ item.icon }}"></i>
            <span>{{ item.title }}</span>
        </a>
        {% endfor %}
        <a href="/logout/" class="nav-link logout">
            <i class="bi bi-box-arrow-right"></i>
            <span data-i18n="logout">Logout</span>
        </a>
    </div>
</div>

7.5 Highlighting the Active Module

The currently active module is highlighted by the CSS class active. The view must set the value active_module in the context:

return render(request, 'template.html', {
    'active_module': 'dashboard',
    ...
})

7.6 Subpages (Submenus)

Modules can define submenu items (subpages). These are displayed in the sidebar under the module when the module is active. The subpages are read from the module's module.json.

7.7 Mobile Sidebar

On mobile devices, the sidebar is hidden by default and can be shown via a button (hamburger menu). The function toggleMobileSidebar() handles showing and hiding.

function toggleMobileSidebar() {
    const sidebar = document.getElementById('sidebar');
    sidebar.classList.toggle('open');
}

The corresponding CSS ensures that the sidebar appears as an overlay on mobile devices:

@media (max-width: 768px) {
    .sidebar {
        left: -250px;
        width: 250px;
    }
    .sidebar.open {
        left: 0;
    }
}
